headline: OpenAI's Jalapeño chip outperforms Nvidia's superchips in AI inference tests
summary: The new AI chip, developed with Broadcom, boasts lower latency and higher throughput, promising faster responses for AI systems.
details: OpenAI has announced its new AI chip, Jalapeño, designed for AI inference tasks. Developed in partnership with Broadcom, this Application-Specific Integrated Circuit (ASIC) aims to deliver both lower latency and higher throughput, addressing a common trade-off in AI systems.

In benchmark tests using InferenceX, Jalapeño demonstrated superior performance compared to Nvidia's GB200 and GB300 superchips. OpenAI reports that Jalapeño achieved 1.5 to 1.9 times more AI work per watt across several models and offered 1.7 to 3.6 times lower end-to-end latency.

These performance improvements translate to faster responses, more responsive AI agents, and more reliable access for users as demand for AI services grows. Richard Ho, OpenAI's VP of hardware, highlighted these benefits during a briefing with reporters.

OpenAI plans to begin deploying Jalapeño in small volumes by the end of this year, with a significant ramp-up in production expected throughout 2027. The company did not specify the exact number of chips planned for deployment next year.

While Jalapeño shows significant promise, OpenAI does not anticipate it replacing its entire chip lineup. The company's compute strategy includes continued collaboration with partners like Nvidia, and OpenAI is already working on the second and third generations of the Jalapeño chip.

OpenAI has announced its new AI chip, Jalapeño, designed for AI inference tasks. Developed in partnership with Broadcom, this Application-Specific Integrated Circuit (ASIC) aims to deliver both lower latency and higher throughput, addressing a common trade-off in AI systems.

OpenAI plans to begin deploying Jalapeño in small volumes by the end of this year, with a significant ramp-up in production expected throughout 2027. The company did not specify the exact number of chips planned for deployment next year.

While Jalapeño shows significant promise, OpenAI does not anticipate it replacing its entire chip lineup. The company's compute strategy includes continued collaboration with partners like Nvidia, and OpenAI is already working on the second and third generations of the Jalapeño chip.
